original_question: Does there exist, in the space of metrics with conical singularities, a (continuous or smooth) family of metrics gt such that g0 is the round metric of the sphere, g1 is the metric from the example above, and σ(gt ) is a decreasing function of t.
target_in_paper: Section 8.7, Question 8.7.1 (Babenko), in the discussion of systolic inequalities on S^2 with conical singularities: the existence of a monotone path for the systolic-area ratio from the round sphere to Croke’s singular two-triangle sphere.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation: it matches Question 8.7.1 almost verbatim, including the space of metrics with conical singularities, the endpoints g0 and g1, and the requirement that σ(gt) decrease along the family.
missing_details: The ambient manifold should be stated explicitly as S^2.

The endpoint g1 should be identified explicitly as the singular metric obtained by gluing two congruent equilateral triangles along their boundaries (the Croke example discussed immediately above the question).
The functional σ(g) should be defined explicitly as σ(g)=area(S^2,g)/sys(S^2,g)^2.
The systole sys(S^2,g) should be defined as the least length of a nontrivial closed geodesic.
To make the family stand-alone, the parameter set should be specified, e.g. a one-parameter family {gt}t∈[0,1].
The draft does not explicitly say that the whole family lies in the space of metrics on S^2 with conical singularities, not just the endpoint g1.
If one wants a fully stand-alone formulation, one should avoid the context-dependent phrase “the example above” and replace it by the explicit geometric description of the example.
refined_question: Let σ(g)=area(S^2,g)/sys(S^2,g)^2, where sys(S^2,g) denotes the least length of a nontrivial closed geodesic of the metric g on S^2. Let g0 be the standard round metric on S^2, and let g1 be the singular metric on S^2 obtained by gluing two congruent equilateral triangles along their boundaries. Does there exist, in the space of metrics on S^2 with conical singularities, a continuous or smooth one-parameter family {gt}t∈[0,1] with g0=g0 and g1=g1 such that t↦σ(gt) is decreasing?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8.7 rather than any earlier conjecture or theorem: Question 8.7.1 is the exact source, and the adjacent paragraph supplies the missing notation and hidden context. Immediately before Question 8.7.1, the paper defines σ(g)=area(S^2,g)/sys(S^2,g)^2 and identifies the relevant singular metric as the sphere obtained by gluing two congruent equilateral triangles along their boundaries. Question 8.7.2 is presented only as “a simpler version” of Question 8.7.1, not as an equivalent reformulation, so no alternate equivalent version should be substituted.
